title: Open/Closed
summary: Add new behaviour by adding code, not by editing a growing switch.

steps.title: The switch that keeps growing
body: decimal Shipping(string method, decimal weight) => method switch

Every new shipping method means editing this function, retesting all of it, and probably editing two other switches on `method` elsewhere in the code. That is the pain the **Open/Closed Principle** targets:
> Software should be **open for extension** but **closed for modification**.
You should be able to add a new shipping method without touching code that already works.

steps.prompt: Product asks for a fourth shipping method, `drone`. With this switch, what must you do?
code: decimal Shipping(string method, decimal weight) => method switch
options: Edit `Shipping` (and any other switch on the method name) and retest it all
steps.explain: The `_` case throws. Every new variant reopens working code, which is exactly what Open/Closed wants to avoid.

steps.title: Strategy instead of switch
body: Put each case behind an interface:
class Standard : IShippingMethod { public decimal Cost(decimal w) => 4m + w * 0.5m; }
class Express  : IShippingMethod { public decimal Cost(decimal w) => 10m + w * 1m; }
class Pickup   : IShippingMethod { public decimal Cost(decimal w) => 0m; }
Code that needs a price takes an `IShippingMethod` and calls `Cost`. Adding `Drone` is one new class; nothing existing changes.

This is not a rule to ban `switch`. A switch that maps *input text* to an object once, at the edge of the program, is fine. The smell is the same switch on a type code repeated through the business logic.

code: IShipping[] options = { new Standard(), new Pickup() };
class Standard : IShipping { public decimal Cost(decimal kg) => 4m + kg * 0.5m; }
class Pickup : IShipping { public decimal Cost(decimal kg) => 0m; }

steps.prompt: Complete the new shipping method without changing any existing code.
code: public decimal __2__(decimal weight) => weight > 5 ? throw new InvalidOperationException() : 15m;

steps.prompt: Your app has `switch (account.Type)` in interest calculation, fee calculation and statement printing. Product wants a new account type. What does Open/Closed suggest?
options: Make each account type a class implementing an interface with `Interest`, `Fee` and `Statement`
Add a fourth `case` to each of the three switches
Replace the switches with `if/else if` chains
Store the type as an `int` instead of a string
steps.explain: Three switches on the same type code is the classic sign. With polymorphism, a new type is one new class.

steps.prompt: Is the code closed for modification when a new variant is added?
items: A list of `IDiscountRule` objects that a checkout loops over
`if (shape is Circle) ... else if (shape is Square) ...`
An enum `ReportType` checked in every report method

steps.title: Replace the switch
prompt: - `class Circle(double radius)`, `class Rectangle(double width, double height)` and `class Triangle(double baseLength, double height)` implementing it (primary constructors are fine)
The tests build shapes and call `Area()`. No `switch` and no type-code string may remain.
solution: public double Area() => Math.PI * radius * radius;
class Rectangle(double width, double height) : IShape
class Triangle(double baseLength, double height) : IShape
template: IShape[] dojoShapes = { new Circle(1), new Rectangle(2, 3), new Triangle(4, 5) };
hints: Each `case` of the switch becomes the body of one class's `Area`.
`class Circle(double radius) : IShape { public double Area() => Math.PI * radius * radius; }`
